Date July 26, 1932

CONFIDENTIAL

Subject (in full) Re attached file

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Quayle

Sir,

Further enquiries have been made re attached file and it appears that the "Fleur de Lys", a millinery and dressmaking establishment situated on Seymour Road adjacent to Bubbling Well Road, was purchased by Mrs. Pearce and Mrs. Tabrum jointly in January 1931, being sold about 3 weeks ago.

I have been unable to ascertain the amount paid for the premises by Mrs. Pearce and Mrs. Tabrum but have received information from a prospective purchaser that price asked for the shop before its sale was $11,000.00.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

J. a. Quayle
Supt.

C.P.

D.C. (Crime)

先生，

就附件档案进行了进一步查询，结果显示，“Fleur de Lys”（百合花饰）是一家位于西摩路（Seymour Road）毗邻静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）的女帽及服装定制店，该店于1931年1月由皮尔斯夫人（Mrs. Pearce）和塔布鲁姆夫人（Mrs. Tabrum）共同购买，并于约三周前售出。

我未能查明皮尔斯夫人和塔布鲁姆夫人购买该房产所支付的金额，但从一位潜在买家处获悉，该店铺在出售前的要价为11,000.00美元。

此致，
敬礼，

J. a. Quayle
警司

C.P.

D.C. (刑事)

Sir,

With reference to the attached case I beg to report having interviewed Liang Zung Nyoh's wife on two occasions on both of which her lawyer Mr. Yui was present. I called her by herself on the first occasion but she had only been in the office a few minutes when her lawyer appeared and constantly interrupted whilst I was questioning her. He appeared to me to be afraid that she would make some statement that would be derogatory to her case. I questioned her closely as to the approximate date she was supposed to have pawned her jewellery and also as to the pawnshops where it was pawned, but she was extremely evasive and even when pressed would give no satisfactory reply. She could not remember even approximately when the pawning took place and stated that she did not know the pawnshops as she had given the jewellery to one Sizu Zung Sung to pawn.

This man has left Shanghai and she does not know where he is at present.

When asked what became of the pawn papers she was very vague and stated that she had sold them but could not give the names of the persons who bought them.

She was also very uncertain of the amount for which the articles were pawned mentioning three different sums during the interview.

When she became confused Mr. Yui stepped in and said he would bring all the information I needed before the 20th July including the letter sent to the father in law Wong Sau Kyung at Wuhu, or else a statement from the latter concerning the loan made by him.

Liang's wife further stated that she had no idea where Tsang

关于附件案件，谨报告我已两次约谈梁宗耀（Liang Zung Nyoh，音译）之妻，两次均有其律师余先生（Mr. Yui，音译）在场。第一次我单独传唤她，但她仅在办公室停留几分钟，其律师便出现，并在我讯问过程中不断打断。在我看来，他似乎担心她会做出对其案件不利的陈述。我就其声称典当首饰的大致日期以及典当行地点对她进行了详细讯问，但她极其回避，即使在追问下也未给出令人满意的答复。她甚至无法大致回忆起典当发生的时间，并称不知道是哪家典当行，因为她已将首饰交给一名叫 Sizu Zung Sung（音译）的人去典当。

此人已离开上海，她目前不知其下落。

当被问及当票下落时，她含糊其辞，称已将其卖出，但无法提供买主姓名。

Sir,

With reference to the attached file I her to report having
interviewed A.I. Henton and questioning him regarding his report
on the matter. I also suggested to him that he might wish to
amplify his report especially with regard to some of the ques-
tions I put to him but he forwarded a memo to me which I have
attached, stating that he had nothing to add to his former report.
I questioned him regarding the man Tsang for whom Henton
allegedly signed the I.O.U.s but he could give me no informa-
tion as to where I would be likely to find this man.
He further stated that in addition to the I.O.U.s written
by him Liang Zung Nyoh also wrote 6 I.O.U.s in Chinese, so that
altogether twelve I.O.U.s for $1000 each were written, but can
give no reason for this. He could not give me any explanation
of how after Tsang had demanded that he write the I.O.U.s they
then came into the possession of Liang who distributed them to
his relatives. He also could not explain why Liang should want
to take the I.O.U. for $6000.00 away and type it after he had
written it out in block letters. He also denies that Liang's
wife was present during the proceedings, despite her statement
which is supported by that of Liang.
I was able to obtain the detectives diaries Liang used
when in the Police, and from a comparison of the handwriting
in them and that on the I.O.U. for $6000.00, the Chinese on the
latter was undoubtedly written by Liang, but I understand it is
only Liang's name and address and does not mention anything
about money.
I again interviewed Liang on 12.7.32 and he adheres to his
original statement and when questioned denied that he knew any—

先生，

关于附件档案，谨报告我已约谈 A.I. Henton，并就其关于此事的报告向他提问。我还建议他可能希望补充其报告，特别是针对我向他提出的一些问题，但他向我提交了一份备忘录（附后），称他对之前的报告无补充内容。
我就亨顿（Henton）据称为其签署借据的那名姓曾（Tsang，音译）的男子向他提问，但他无法向我提供可能在何处找到此人的信息。
他还表示，除了他写的借据外，梁宗耀还用中文写了6张借据，因此总共写了十二张面值各为1000美元的借据，但他无法说明原因。他无法解释为何在曾要求他写下借据后，这些借据会落入梁的手中，并由梁分发给其亲属。他也无法解释为何梁在用手写印刷体写下6000.00美元的借据后，又要将其拿走并打字处理。他还否认梁妻当时在场，尽管梁妻有此陈述，且得到梁的佐证。
我取得了梁在警队服役时使用的侦探日记，通过对比日记中的笔迹与6000.00美元借据上的笔迹，可以确定后者上的中文无疑由梁所写，但我了解到那上面只有梁的姓名和地址，并未提及任何关于金钱的内容。
我于1932年7月12日再次约谈梁，他坚持其原始陈述，并在被问及时否认认识任何——

when the arrangements for the loan were made. He states that
the only person present was his wife, which is also confirmed
by her attached statement.
He also stated that had he been a free man no such charge
would have been brought against Henton & he would prefer to
lose the money rather than cause any trouble over the matter.
He denied he possessed any title deeds for land whatso-
ever and said that if he had any and wanted money any bank
would advance him cash against them. He also stated that he
could neither read, write or speak English.
From the above enquiries it will be seen that it is a mat-
ter of conjecture as to who is telling the truth. Henton is
an experienced man having served a long time on the S.M.P. and
it seems difficult to imagine he would have acted with such
stupidity as he alleges he did.
On the other hand Liang Zung Nyoh is a very clever indivi-
dual with considerable experience of foreigners, having in addi-
tion to his Police Service been in France with the coolie corps,
and it is extremely difficult to imagine him acting so innocent-
ly. His statement, however, is corroborated by his wife who
appears to be a simple country type of woman and on his side it
can be said that Henton can give no explanation as to how his
I.O.U.s came into the possession of Liang's relatives when they
were supposed to be made out for a man named Tsang.
I am, Sir,
Yours obediently
Jn. Doyle
Supt.

名叫曾（Tsang，音译）的人，也否认在安排贷款时有其他人在场。他称当时在场的唯一人员是其妻子，这也由其附后的陈述所证实。
他还表示，如果他是一个自由人，就不会对亨顿（Henton）提出此类指控，他宁愿损失这笔钱，也不愿就此事项引起任何麻烦。
他否认拥有任何土地契据，并称如果他有任何契据并需要资金，任何银行都会据此向他预支现金。他还表示，他既不会读、也不会写或说英语。
从上述调查可以看出，谁在说实话纯属猜测。亨顿是一名经验丰富的人员，在上海公共租界工部局警务处服役已久，很难想象他会像他声称的那样愚蠢行事。
另一方面，梁宗耀是一个非常聪明的人，拥有丰富的与外国人打交道的经验，除了在警队服役外，还曾在法国随华工军团服役，很难想象他会表现得如此无辜。然而，他的陈述得到了其妻子的佐证，她看起来是一位单纯的乡村妇女类型；站在梁的一边可以说，亨顿无法解释为何他的借据会落入梁的亲属手中，而这些借据本应是为一位名叫曾的人出具的。
此致，
敬礼，
Jn. Doyle
警司

Made by D.I. Chapman Forwarded by Supt. Quayle

Sir,

Re attached statement taken at S.M. Gaol, Liang Zung Nyoh
states that at the time of his arrest, one I.O.U. for $1,000.00
was in his home, the remaining five being in the hands of his
relations from whom the money was borrowed. He himself has had
nothing to do with bringing forward these I.O.U.s. He further
states that he has never possessed any title deeds for land,
and volunteered to be questioned before S.I. Henton on the whole
matter. He never received the $600.00 which Henton was supposed
to be borrowing on the strength of Liang's guarantee, and which
was intended to be used as payment of interest on the $6000.00
loan.

I am, Sir,

At 10 a.m. on June 27, 1932, D.I. Sherman came to the Gaol and
again questioned me about the $6000.00. The truth of the matter
has already been given in my last statement. I have never
borrowed $6000.00 for myself. I do not know who Tsang is supposed

以下是梁宗耀（Liang Zung Nyoh，音译），前3.D.3，编号2，山东籍人士的陈述，由我 Clark Tsu Vi Gi（音译）于1932年6月27日在华德路监狱取得，并由

1932年6月27日上午10时，侦探督察谢尔曼（Sherman）来到监狱，再次就6,000.00美元一事对我进行讯问。事实真相已在我上一次的陈述中给出。我从未为自己借过6,000.00美元。我不知道所谓的曾（Tsang，音译）是谁，我也从未请求亨顿先生为我担任担保人。1931年1月或2月间，亨顿先生回到上海后，来找我，说他打算向其在亚洲石油公司（A.P.J.）任职的朋友借款600.00美元。他请求我担任担保人。我想既然我已经为他借过6,000.00美元，再为他担保600.00美元也无妨，于是我同意了，并在他用英文书写的一张纸上签了名并盖了章。由于我不懂英文，我不知道纸上写了什么。

Subject (in full) Liang Zung Nyoeh.

Made by J.L. O. Henton. Forwarded by

Sir,

I beg to state that during the month of December 1929 I was transferred from Kio Lin Road Station to Louza. At this time, I was in the C.I.D. It was at the latter named station that I came in close contact with D.D.C.No.2 Liang Zung Nyoeh, who was also attached to Louza Station.

We sometimes worked together on cases and the impression I gathered was that he was very clever, and was one of the smartest Chinese detectives I had met.

On a day which I remember rightly was about the end of March, Liang Zung Nyoeh approached me and asked me if I would stand guarantor for $6,000.00 which he wanted to borrow from a friend. The money he said was wanted very urgently as he had an offer to buy some land for which he had been negotiating for some time. Some of the money was to be sent to his father in North China to enable him to purchase his own farm, which was now for sale and was likely to be purchased by someone else if he, Liang Zung Nyoeh, did not send the money.

I refused to stand guarantor and the matter was dropped for the time being. Liang Zung Nyoeh however called me almost daily regarding this matter, I however refused to be connected with borrowing money.

Sometime in June 1930, Liang Zung Nyoeh came to me in Louza Station and said if I would stand guarantor for $6000.00, he would give me the title deeds to some land which was valued at $10,000.00 and I could hold these deeds until he returned my I.O.Us. Furthermore he would give me the deeds that day & I could take them to a Chinese lawyer to be examined and valued. This appeared to me to be quite straight, and as he appeared to me to be in some sort of financial trouble, I said I would help him and stand guarantor.

I took the papers and kept them for three or four days, intending to give Liang Zung Nyoeh the impression that I was having them examined. I did not have them examined however but locked them up in my trunk. By arrangement with Liang Zung Nyoeh, I visited his home some days later to sign the papers. I first asked him however why he did not give the papers to the person from whom he intended borrowing the money, and he said he did not wish anyone besides myself to know that he owned land. We then went into a small side room where he introduced me to the person from whom he was going to borrow the money and whom he introduced to me as Tsang, a merchant who resided in Frenchtown. I then signed a paper to the effect that I would be guarantor for $6000.00 to Liang Zung Nyoeh. This the above named Tsang who spoke and read English would not accept and asked that I write six direct I.O.Us. for $1000.00 each, as the money was to be repaid to him by Liang Zung Nyoeh one thousand dollars at a time.

具报人 J.L. O. Henton。转呈人

阁下：

谨呈，本人于1929年12月间由乔林路（Kio Lin Road）巡捕房调往老闸（Louza）巡捕房。当时，本人在刑事侦缉处（C.I.D.）任职。正是在后一名称的巡捕房，本人与同样隶属于老闸巡捕房的副探目第2号梁宗岳有了密切接触。

我们有时共同办案，本人对他的印象是他非常聪明，是本人所遇见的最精明的华籍侦探之一。

记得大约在3月底的一天，梁宗岳接近本人，问本人是否愿意为他向朋友借款6,000.00美元作保。他说急需这笔钱，因为他有一笔购买土地的报价，而该土地他已洽谈了一段时间。部分款项需汇给他在华北的父亲，以便其购买自家农场，该农场现已出售，如果梁宗岳不汇款，很可能被他人买走。

本人拒绝作保，此事暂时搁置。然而，梁宗岳几乎每天都就此事来找本人，但本人始终拒绝卷入借贷金钱之事。

1930年6月某时，梁宗岳来到老闸巡捕房找本人，称如果本人愿为6,000.00美元作保，他将把价值10,000.00美元的一些土地的地契交给本人，本人可持有这些地契直至他归还本人的借据。此外，他当天就会交出地契，本人可将其带给中国律师进行查验和估值。这在本人看来相当正当，且鉴于他似乎陷入某种财务困境，本人表示愿意帮助他并为之作保。

本人收下文件并保留了三四天，意在给梁宗岳留下本人正在查验文件的印象。然而本人并未实际查验，而是将其锁在手提箱中。按照与梁宗岳的约定，几天后本人前往其家中签署文件。本人首先问他为何不把文件交给拟向其借款的人，他说他不希望除本人以外的任何人知道拥有土地。随后我们进入一间小侧室，他向本人介绍了拟向其借款的人，并称其为曾（Tsang），一位居住在法租界（Frenchtown）的商人。于是本人签署了一份文件，大意是为梁宗岳的6,000.00美元借款作保。上述那位懂英语读写能力的曾先生不肯接受此文件，要求本人直接出具六张借据，每张1,000.00美元，因为梁宗岳将分次每次偿还他一千元。

I and Liang Zung Nyoeh then wrote what I was given to understand
were I.O.Us. for six thousand dollars in Chinese. I then wrote
I.O.Us. for six thousand dollars and gave them to Liang Zung
Nyoeh. Shortly after I left the premises but did not see
the I.O.Us. handed over to Tommy, nor did I see any money paid
to Liang Zung Nyoeh. Liang Zung Nyoeh first explained that
he did not wish anyone not even his wife to know that he had
borrowed money, and asked me to keep the transaction a secret.

Before I went on leave in July 1930 Liang Zung Nyoeh gave
me a present of a silverpumpkin which I valued at about $300.00.
The pumpkin was inscribed "To my friend Mr. Mutton" and Liang
Zung Nyoeh when giving it to me stated that it was for helping
him to borrow the money.

About 1 week after I had returned from long leave, Liang
Zung Nyoeh visited me and stated that whilst I had been on
long leave, he had lost nearly all his money through gambling
and was therefore unable to get back our I.O.Us. I pointed
out that I still had the title deeds which I should continue
to hold until my I.O.Us. were returned. Liang Zung Nyoeh then
visited me daily always insisting that he could not get our
I.O.Us. until he sold the land to which I held the deeds.
As this seemed to be the only way of getting back my I.O.Us.,
I finally told Liang that if he would sign me one I.O.U. for
$500.00, I would return him his title deeds. To this he
readily consented and on the evening of April 6th I printed
an I.O.U. in English which I told him to type out in English
so that he could sign and chop it in my presence. This he
did and the following day I visited his home at Chengtu Road
with the title deeds which I returned to him after he signed
an I.O.U. to me with his name, address and chop, and which I
still hold.

The following day Liang Zung Nyoeh came to me and said
he was very sorry, but had made a mistake in the chop on my
I.O.U. and asked me if I would return it in order that he
could put on the correct chop. I refused and the next day
had the chop and signature examined and found them correct.
I was then suspicious and pressed Liang Zung Nyoeh for my
I.O.Us. Some days later when I again saw Liang, I assured
him I had destroyed his I.O.U. because I thought him honest,
and then he stated that he had redeemed my I.O.Us. whilst I
was on leave and had destroyed them some months previously.

Some time after this he was arrested and then some of my
I.O.Us. turned up. The wife of Liang visited me at my home in
Wayside Road with three of my I.O.Us. and wanted $3000.00.
I told her to visit her husband who would explain everything.
After this there was a constant stream of Liang's informers
visiting me for money which I stopped by threatening to take
the next one to the Police Station. Liang's wife continued
to visit me but finally stopped when she found no money
forthcoming.

随后，本人与梁宗岳写下了据本人理解是中文的六千元借据。接着本人又写了六千元的借据并交给梁宗岳。不久后本人离开该处，但未见到借据移交给汤米（Tommy），也未见到有任何钱款支付给梁宗岳。梁宗岳起初解释说，他不希望任何人，甚至包括他的妻子，知道他借了钱，并要求本人对此交易保密。

在本人于1930年7月休长假之前，梁宗岳送给本人一个银质南瓜作为礼物，本人估值约为300.00美元。南瓜上刻有“赠予我的朋友 Mutton 先生”字样，梁宗岳在赠送时称这是为了感谢本人帮他借钱。

在本人休完长假回来约一周后，梁宗岳来访，称在本人休长假期间，他因赌博输掉了几乎所有的钱，因此无法取回我们的借据。本人指出，本人仍持有地契，在借据归还之前将继续持有。此后梁宗岳每日来访，坚持称在卖出本人持有地契的土地之前，他无法取回我们的借据。由于这似乎是收回本人借据的唯一途径，本人最终告诉梁，如果他给本人签署一张500.00美元的借据，本人就将地契还给他。他欣然同意，4月6日晚，本人打印了一份英文借据，让他用打字机打出英文版，以便他在本人面前签字盖章。他照办了，次日本人携带地契前往他在成都路（Chengtu Road）的住所，在他签署了一张写有姓名、地址并加盖印章的借据交予本人后，本人将地契还给了他，该借据本人至今仍持有。

翌日，梁宗岳来找本人，称非常抱歉，但在本人借据上的印章弄错了，问本人能否归还借据以便他盖上正确的印章。本人拒绝了，并在第二天对印章和签名进行了查验，发现无误。此时本人起了疑心，便向梁宗岳催讨本人的借据。几天后，当本人再次见到梁时，本人向他保证，出于对他诚实的信任，本人已销毁了他的借据，随后他声称在本人休假期间已赎回了本人的借据，并于数月前将其销毁。

此后不久，他被逮捕，接着本人的一些借据出现了。梁的妻子带着本人的三张借据来到本人在威赛德路（Wayside Road）的家中，索要3,000.00美元。本人让她去见她的丈夫，他会解释一切。此后，梁的眼线络绎不绝地来找本人要钱，本人以威胁将下一个带来的人送往巡捕房为止住了他们。梁的妻子继续来访，但最终因发现无钱可拿而停止。

This woman alleged that through her relations with Henton
she had become enceinte and wanted to go to Japan to give birth
to the child.
She stated that if the money was not forthcoming she
would tell her husband of the affair and he would report it
to the Commissioner of Police and ensure Henton's dismissal
from the Force.
Henton then went to Liang Zung Nyoh and told him of the
trouble he was in and asked Liang to assist him in raising
the money to pay the woman off. Liang agreed and approached
two of his relatives named Woo Tsong Mei and Wong Sau Kyung,
the former being a house owner and the latter the proprietor
of an exchange shop. From them he obtained the sum of $5500.00,
$3000.00 being paid by Woo Tsong Mei and $2500.00 by Wong Sau
Kyung.
A further sum of $500.00 was contributed by his wife making
in all $6000.00.
The arrangement was that Liang Zung Nyoh was to be the mid-
dleman in the transaction and at the end of Henton's long leave
the money was to be repaid together with $600.00 interest which
money Henton stated he intended to obtain from his superannuation.
Henton then gave Liang Zung Nyoh six I.O.U.s for $1000.00
each and these were handed to the above mentioned Chinese. The
reason for making out 6 I.O.U.s was stated to be that when Henton
obtained $1000.00 he could pay it to his creditors and have one
of the I.O.U.s returned instead of waiting until he had collected
the full amount of $6000.00.
When Henton returned from long leave Liang Zung Nyoh approach-
ed him regarding the payment of the interest but was unable to
obtain any satisfaction.

1931 年 1 月或 2 月，亨顿（Henton）先生回到上海，住在麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）的一家寄宿公寓。我曾到该地址拜访他，问他何时还钱。他说他一两天后会来看我。有一天，他带着妻子来看我，并告诉我他妻子的叔叔非常富有，因此我不必担心这笔钱。

后来他被调往杨树浦巡捕房，我曾去那里看望过他。第二天他到我家来看我。他告诉我，他打算向一位在工部局警务处（A.P.C.）任职的朋友借款 600.00 美元，并请我作担保人。他要我给他一张白纸，让我在上面签名并盖章。我照做了，但他说他写错了一个字，让我在另一张纸上重新签名盖章。这次碰巧我又盖错了章，于是有人让我再拿一张纸。之后我下楼去吃午饭，将那两张无用的纸留在桌上。随后，亨顿先生未告辞便从后门离开了我家。当我回到楼上房间时，我

On one occasion I went to visit Mr. Henton at Boone Road.
He told me that he could alter the paper on which I fixed my sig-
nature and chop as a guarantor to an I.O.U. issued by me for any
amount he wished to write.

After I was detained in the Sinza Station cells, Mr. Hen-

red to the Traffic Office. I asked him about the money, but he
said that he would refund the money if my wife returned him the
6 I.D.U.s. I do not know the rest. The above is my true
statement.

我被关进新闸巡捕房（Sinza Station）拘留所期间，亨顿先生曾来探望过我一次。他告诉我他现在已调至交通股。我向他问起那笔钱的事，但他说如果我妻子退还那 6 张国际驾驶执照（I.D.U.s），他就会还钱。其余情况我不了解。以上是我的真实陈述。
